newsitem.title: USA: Bacteria-spiked doughnuts sicken 13 in Dallas.
newsitem.headline: Bacteria-spiked doughnuts sicken 13 in Dallas.

text.p: FBI agents were called in on Monday to investigate the contamination of doughnuts and muffins with a rare strain of bacteria that left 13 Dallas hospital employees seriously ill last month.

Officials at the St. Paul Medical Centre said the doughnuts and muffins were ordered from outside, implanted with a bacteria culture known as shigella dysenteriae that had disappeared from a laboratory refrigerator and left in a staff room for lab workers to eat.

An electronic-mail note was sent to lab employees telling them the food was there for all who wanted it, yet officials have so far been unable to determine who ordered the snacks, who contaminated them or who encouraged workers to eat them.

"The investigation is ongoing and ... we referred the matter to the FBI," said hospital spokesman Brian Levinson. "We want to determine who brought the dougnuts in and what the motive for the contamination may have been."
Thirteen employees suffered severe diarrhoea and stomach cramps after eating the food and five were hospitalized. All have since recovered.
Levinson said shigella dysenteriae was a rare strain of bacteria usually found in developing countries.
The hospital's laboratory, like those at many major medical centres, keeps a variety of stock bacteria cultures on hand for educational and testing purposes.
